solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Place one must get out of party game

parts.words: Place one must get out of
parts.note: to dodge something is to get out of it, so the phrase describing a spot one must escape points to the verb
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: Someone stuck at a dreary party wants to leave as fast as they can.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the very end; 'party game' reads as one phrase, but 'party' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodgeball is a team sport in which players throw balls at opponents, who try to avoid being hit.

clue.text: Reportedly held back on the way to hell

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a dammed river is held back

explanation.surface: A reported delay on a journey to the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: The damned are souls condemned to eternal punishment in hell.

clue.text: Olympian cheated when swimming without permit

indicators.note: without means outside, so the anagram goes around the other piece
swimming means the letters of cheated are moving about

parts.note: to let is to permit

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete broke the rules in the pool without a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges CHEATED to DECATHE, which goes 'without' (outside) LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A decathlete competes in the ten-event decathlon, a classic Olympic event.

clue.text: Vote in referendum primarily about something negative?

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of referendum

parts.note: on can mean about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A referendum ballot that is mainly about rejecting something.
explanation.definitionFit: An electron carries a negative electric charge, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Hours sunk into soaring piece of music that's improvised

indicators.note: sunk into means the letter for hours is dropped inside the other piece
in a down clue soaring means rising, so the word for a piece of music reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a coda is the closing passage of a piece of music

explanation.surface: Hours of practice poured into a soaring musical passage that was made up on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soaring' sits right beside 'piece of music', so only CODA is turned up, giving ADOC; 'sunk into' then drops H into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ad hoc means arranged for a particular purpose, without planning, so made up as needed.

clue.text: Awful mark erasable — with this?

indicators.note: awful suggests a mess, so the letters of erasable are jumbled

parts.note: M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A dreadful blemish can be removed with this tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: 'Awful' scrambles the letters of 'erasable' (to LASERBEA), and the M from 'mark' is placed after them although printed first.
explanation.definitionFit: Laser beams are used to remove tattoos and blemishes, so a mark becomes erasable with one.

clue.text: A sharp pain — darn!

definitions.meaning: a sudden sharp pain in the side
to darn is to mend with ..., so a ... is what darning makes

explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is a sharp pain from running, and also a single loop of thread used in sewing or darning.

clue.text: Ladies' man is regularly head over heels in this region

indicators.note: head over heels means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read upward
regularly takes every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: A womaniser falls head over heels for someone in this part of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks AISA from 'Ladies' man'; 'head over heels' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast region of the world.

clue.text: Satisfied with hotel signs I would say

parts.note: met as in met demands means satisfied
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to ink a contract is to sign it

explanation.surface: A guest pleased with a hotel's signage offers an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Methinks is an archaic expression meaning it seems to me.

clue.text: Performer, in part, is terrific

indicators.note: 'in' tells us the answer sits inside the words that follow it in the clue

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict that a performer is terrific in one particular role.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Play live match moved outside

indicators.note: the rearranged letters of match are placed outside, around, the word for live
the letters of match are moved around into a new order

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A live sports fixture has been rescheduled to be played outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb, but it is the definition, a stage play; 'moved' scrambles the letters to MACTH and 'outside' wraps that around the word for live.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Shakespeare's tragedy about a Scottish thane who murders his way to the throne.

clue.text: Cyclist's close with a head coach

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so the final letter of cyclist is taken

parts.note: 'a head' means per person, which is each

explanation.surface: A cycling coach at the end of a race, with each rider getting individual attention.
explanation.definitionFit: To coach someone is to train or instruct them, which is to teach.

clue.text: Hurry back around New York, perhaps, to get vehicle

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the word for New York
back tells us the word for hurry is read in reverse

parts.note: to race is to hurry
New York is one example of a US state

explanation.surface: Someone dashes back through New York to collect a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New York, perhaps' is a definition by example of a US state; 'back' gives ECAR and 'around' puts that round the state.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a British name for a station wagon, a car with a long rear load space.

clue.text: Country curses bad weather

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of annoyance, like curses
rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: People in a country grumbling about the dreadful weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island nation in the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Possibly made perfect show on book in a hurry

parts.note: to air something is to show it publicly
rushed means done in a hurry

explanation.surface: A show staged hastily after a book, possibly made perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: An airbrushed photo has been retouched to remove flaws, perhaps making it look flawless.

clue.text: Person fighting to unwrap a classic film, for example

indicators.note: unwrapping something removes its outer covering, so the first and last letters of the word go

parts.note: a soldier is a person who fights

explanation.surface: A war film about a soldier being opened up as a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to unwrap' strips the outer letters S and R from SOLDIER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is something old but still enjoyed, such as a vintage film or song.

clue.text: Oscar follows blokes into dodgy bar having left work

indicators.note: into places these letters inside the word for a dodgy bar

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable bar

indicators.note: follows puts the letter for Oscar after the blokes

parts.note: men are blokes
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar winner joins some lads in a seedy bar after leaving the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like the job being left, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime novel is a cheap, sensational work of popular fiction.

clue.text: Mug a writer

explanation.definitionFit: A stein is an earthenware beer tankard, and Stein is also the surname of the writer Gertrude Stein.

clue.text: Philosopher king gets hold of rocket ultimately for space programme

indicators.note: gets hold of means takes inside

parts.note: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French philosopher

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of rocket

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A philosopher-king seizes a rocket for a space mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is a long-running science-fiction TV series set in space.

clue.text: Primate's brother's inviting one in

indicators.note: inviting someone (in) takes them inside, so the letter for one goes inside the other piece

parts.note: 'Lor', short for Lord, is an exclamation like brother!; the 's adds S
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A churchman's brother hospitably asks someone into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Primate looks like a bishop; 'brother' is the exclamation 'Oh brother!', matched by Lor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loris is a small, slow-moving nocturnal primate of South and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Crazy golf followed by bumpy mule ride

indicators.note: followed by puts the second piece after the first
crazy says the letters of golf are jumbled
bumpy says the letters of mule are shaken up

explanation.surface: A round of crazy golf, then a jolting donkey ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' turns GOLF into LOGF; 'bumpy' turns MULE into LUME, which is 'followed by' placement.
explanation.definitionFit: A log flume is a theme-park water ride in log-shaped boats.

clue.text: Cuban steps over short snake first

indicators.note: first says the snake comes before the other piece
short means the last letter of the snake is cut off

parts.note: a mamba is a venomous African snake
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Dance steps, with a snake shortened and the order of moves given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuban steps' is the definition, not 'Cuban'; 'short' docks the snake's last letter and 'first' puts the docked snake ahead of the cricket over.
explanation.definitionFit: The mambo is a Latin dance that originated in Cuba.

clue.text: Thinner expert has style

parts.note: an ace is an expert
tone can mean style or character, as in the tone of a place

explanation.surface: A slimmer expert who also has style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' reads as slimmer, but here it is the noun for a solvent.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a solvent used as paint thinner and nail polish remover.

clue.text: Energy about a brass band's sound

indicators.note: about means the word for energy goes around the other piece

parts.note: oomph means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A lively brass band plays with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oompah is the rhythmic deep sound of tubas in a brass band.

clue.text: Kind offer

definitions.meaning: to offer, as with a resignation or bid

explanation.definitionFit: Tender as an adjective means gentle and caring; as a verb it means to put forward formally.

clue.text: Feel snout working when using it?

definitions.text: Feel snout working when using it?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician feels their nose busy while playing an unusual instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose flute is a wind instrument blown through the nostril, so the snout is working when it is played.

clue.text: Exercise set: one's somersaulting

indicators.note: somersaulting means flipping over, so the letters read in reverse

parts.note: to put is to set down
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: A gymnast performs a set in which they somersault.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-up is an abdominal exercise of raising the torso from lying down.

clue.text: Symbol of bear market's beginning

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear

indicators.note: the beginning of market is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bear as the emblem of a falling stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear market' looks like a stock-trading term, but bear is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an object or animal serving as an emblem of a group.

clue.text: Set up wrong sort of socialist

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means placed upward, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A socialist of the wrong sort has been framed.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is informal for Trotskyist, a follower of Leon Trotsky's brand of socialism.

clue.text: Mad man admits it hurts

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Ted is a man's name
ouch is what one says when it hurts

explanation.surface: A furious man confesses he is in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Touched is an informal word for slightly crazy.

clue.text: English house having no heart for environmental terrorism

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so one of the central letters is removed

parts.note: a cottage is a small house

explanation.surface: An English home gutted by eco-activists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no heart' takes one middle T out of COTTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecotage is sabotage carried out in the name of protecting the environment.

clue.text: Perceptive observer's article about one way of voting

indicators.note: the article goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's main editorial article
I is the Roman numeral for one
PR is proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: A sharp-eyed commentator writes about an electoral system.
explanation.definitionFit: A lip-reader understands speech by watching mouth movements closely, so is a perceptive watcher.
